events.title: Collision with the iceberg
events.description: Moments after the lookouts report an iceberg right ahead and the helm is put hard over, the ship strikes the ice on her starboard side forward, below the waterline. First Officer Murdoch closes the watertight doors and Captain Smith comes to the bridge.
events.note: 11.40 p.m. ship's time in the British report; the US report gives 11:46 and individual accounts range from 11:40 to 11:45. The contact lasted under ten seconds.

events.title: Water enters boiler rooms 6 and 5
events.description: Water comes through the ship's side about two feet above the stokehold plates in No. 6 boiler room and in the forward starboard coal bunker of No. 5.
events.note: Leading Fireman Barrett, British Inquiry, Q1868–1874 and Q1917–1921, as cited by the report.

events.title: Engines stopped
events.description: The engines are noticed to have stopped. Fourth Officer Boxhall goes below to inspect the forward passenger spaces.
events.note: Sequence reconstructed by Halpern from Boxhall (Q15573), Dillon (Q3716–3729) and Lightoller (Q13743). The engines turned slowly ahead again for a short time before stopping for good at about 11:46.

events.title: Forepeak tank filling
events.description: Crew find air being forced out of the forepeak tank as it fills, and ice lying on the forward well deck.
events.note: Hemming (Q17716) and Haines, as cited by Halpern. The forepeak above the tank stayed dry at this stage.

events.title: Steam blows off at the funnels
events.description: With the engines stopped, the boilers begin venting steam through the safety valves at the funnels, with a noise that hampers speech on deck and wireless reception.
events.note: Start time from the chart of Fitch, Layton and Wormstedt, whose supporting argument was not located in the parts read. The steam stopped at about 12:58.

events.title: List of about 5° to starboard
events.description: The inclinometer in the wheelhouse shows a list of about five degrees to starboard, five to ten minutes after the collision.
events.note: Quartermaster Hichens (US Inquiry, p. 450–451), as cited by Halpern, whose heeling-moment calculation gives 5.15°. The time is approximate.

events.title: Water rising in the forward compartments
events.description: About ten minutes after the collision the water stands about eight feet above the double bottom in No. 6 boiler room and about seven feet deep in No. 1 hold. The carpenter reports to the bridge that the ship is making water.
events.note: Barrett (Q1926, Q1937) and Poingdestre (Q2821–2822) in the report; Boxhall (Q15367–15370) read directly. Halpern reads Barrett's eight feet as the low starboard side under the list.

events.title: Stokehold lights fail briefly
events.description: The lights go out in the stokeholds of boiler rooms 5 and 4; lamps are sent for. They come back about ten minutes later.
events.note: Barrett (Q1957–1961, Q2007–2014) and Cavell (Q4215–4218), as cited by Halpern; both times are his reconstruction.

events.title: Mail hold flooding
events.description: Boxhall finds the mail hold flooding, with the water within about two feet of G deck and rising.
events.location: No. 3 hold, Orlop and G decks
events.note: Boxhall, British Inquiry, Q15374–15376.

events.title: Water reaches G deck forward
events.description: Water comes onto G deck around No. 1 hatch, and flooding is seen in the first-class baggage room.
events.location: No. 1 and No. 3 holds, G deck
events.note: Symons (Q11354–11356), Johnston (Q3395–3397) and Wheat (Q10901–10918), as cited by Halpern, who derives a trim of 0.8° from Symons's observation. The observations are established; the time is approximate.

events.title: Officers called; all hands to the boats
events.description: Boxhall reports the flooding of the mail room to Captain Smith and is sent to call the off-duty officers; the boatswain calls all hands to the boats. Water is coming up No. 1 hatch into the firemen's quarters. The clock change planned for midnight is not made.
events.note: Boxhall (Q15377–15380) read directly; Lee (Q2455–2485) in the report; Pitman and Symons as cited by Halpern. Whether any clock had been put back is a separate, debated question recorded in the time reference.

events.title: Order to uncover the boats
events.description: The order is given to uncover the lifeboats. Covers are taken off while steam roars from the funnels.
events.note: "About 12.5" in the British report; Boxhall (Q15384–15385) and Pitman (Q14949–14955) as cited by Halpern. The event is established; the time is approximate.

events.title: Water nears E deck forward
events.description: Water is within six steps of E deck on the stairs leading down to the mail room. Captain Smith and Thomas Andrews return from inspecting the flooded spaces.
events.note: Stewardess Robinson (Q13277–13283), as cited by Halpern, who derives a trim of about 1.8° from it. The inspections by Smith and Andrews are reconstructed from stewards' sightings and have no clock time.

events.title: Boats swung out; passengers called up
events.description: Captain Smith orders the boats swung out and passengers called on deck with lifebelts.
events.note: Halpern places the order at about 12:12 (Hichens, Q1041–1043; Ismay).

alternatives.position: Order to swing out given at 12.20.

events.title: Andrews judges the ship lost
events.description: Thomas Andrews tells Captain Smith that the ship cannot be saved and has perhaps an hour to an hour and a half left.
events.note: Reconstructed by Halpern from second-hand accounts (a passenger put it about 45 minutes after the collision; Boxhall, Q15610). No witness gave a clock time.

events.title: Water on E deck forward
events.description: A wooden bulkhead gives way and about three feet of water enters the seamen's quarters on E deck.
events.location: E deck forward, over No. 2 hold
events.note: Poingdestre (Q2842–2858): "about 40 minutes after" the collision in the report, 45 minutes for Halpern, who derives a trim of 2.6° from it.

events.title: Women and children to the boats; call for assistance
events.description: Captain Smith orders women and children into the boats, then goes to the Marconi room and orders the call for assistance.
events.note: Bride (Q16503–16510) read directly. Halpern gives about 12:25; the British report says "about 12.30".

events.title: Boxhall's position taken to the wireless cabin
events.description: Boxhall shows Captain Smith the position he has worked out, 41°46′N, 50°14′W, and takes it to the wireless cabin. It replaces the first position sent and lies about 13 nautical miles west of where the wreck was found.
events.note: Boxhall (Q15388–15391) read directly. The time is back-calculated by Halpern from the message logged at 10:35 p.m. New York time.

events.title: Engineers work to bring pumps forward
events.description: The watertight doors aft of the engine room are ordered open so that a portable suction pipe can be carried forward; it is connected in No. 4 boiler room by about 1:35.
events.location: Engine room; shaft tunnels; boiler room 4
events.note: Greaser Scott (Q5600–5604: "quarter to one") and Wilding (Q20682–20686), as cited by Halpern. The report notes that the pumps, about 1,700 tons an hour in all, could not have coped.

events.title: Rowe told to bring distress signals
events.description: Quartermaster Rowe, on the poop, telephones the bridge to report a boat in the water and is told to bring more distress signals forward.
events.note: Rowe (Q17614–17624) read directly. He timed it at 12:25; Wormstedt, Fitch and Behe take that as reckoned 23 minutes back, hence 12:48.

events.title: Water flows from E deck to F deck
events.description: Water is seen flowing down the first-class stairs from E deck to F deck, just abaft bulkhead F: it has risen above the tops of the forward watertight bulkheads.
events.location: E and F decks, over boiler room 4
events.note: Assistant Second Steward Wheat (Q10956–10972), as cited by Halpern, who gives 12:45–12:50 in 2017 and 12:55 in 2023 and derives a trim of 3.2°.

events.title: Rockets seen from the Californian
events.description: On the SS Californian, stopped in the ice to the north, Second Officer Stone sees the first of eight white rockets over a steamer to the south-east.
events.note: Stone (Q7829–7841) read directly: about 12:45 by the Californian's clock, 12 minutes behind Titanic's on Halpern's alignment. The sighting is established; the alignment is estimated.

events.title: Steam stops blowing off
events.description: The roar of escaping steam at the funnels ceases.
events.note: Argued by Fitch, Layton and Wormstedt in their 2026 study.

events.title: Rush of water in boiler room 5
events.description: A rush of water through the pass between the boilers drives the men out of No. 5 boiler room.
events.note: Barrett (Q1969, Q2038–2041, Q2348–2349). Halpern follows Barrett's own best guess of about 1:10.

alternatives.position: A bunker door gave way about an hour after the collision, that is about 12:40.

events.title: List gone; water in boiler room 4
events.description: The starboard list has disappeared and the ship is upright before beginning to list to port. Water is rising through the stokehold plates at the forward end of No. 4 boiler room, and from a boat the sea is seen up to the second row of portholes under the ship's name.
events.note: Ward ("She was not listing at all", US Inquiry p. 599), Symons (Q11490) and Cavell (Q4248–4265) as cited by Halpern; Dillon (Q3811, Q3913) in the report. Halpern derives a trim of 4.0°.

events.title: Stokers and greasers ordered on deck
events.description: Most of the remaining firemen, trimmers and greasers are ordered up from the stokeholds and engine rooms with lifebelts. Boiler rooms 3, 2 and 1 and the engine rooms are still dry. The engineers remain at work below.
events.note: Dillon (Q3795, Q3811), Scott (Q5838–5839) and Threlfall all give about 1:20. No engineer officer survived.

events.title: Forecastle deck not yet under
events.description: Seen from the boats, the forecastle deck is still above water.
events.note: Lookout Lee, Q2541.

events.title: Propellers partly out of the water
events.description: From a boat astern, the propellers are seen about half out of the water.
events.note: Boatswain's Mate Nichols's account, as cited by Halpern, whose trim curve gives about 5° at this time.

events.title: Forward well deck awash; heavy list to port
events.description: The forward well deck is awash and the ship has a marked list to port. The forecastle head is close to the water but not yet submerged.
events.note: Bride reporting Phillips (Q16548–16553) read directly; Lightoller (Q14081) in the report. Halpern derives a trim of 5.5° and a list of about 10° to port.

events.title: Wireless operators released
events.description: Captain Smith tells the wireless operators they have done their duty and can do no more. Phillips continues to transmit.
events.note: Bride's report of 27 April, as cited by Halpern, set against the last message heard by Carpathia at 11:55 p.m. New York time.

events.title: Forecastle going under; water on A deck
events.description: As the last boat is lowered from the davits, the forecastle head is going under, the forward well deck is submerged and water is coming onto A deck on the port side and up the stairway under the Boat deck.
events.location: Forecastle; A deck, port side forward
events.note: Lightoller (Q14018–14027) in the report; Bright, Rowe and Woolner as cited by Halpern and by Wormstedt, Fitch and Behe. The clock time is approximate.

events.title: Electrical power failing; wireless cabin abandoned
events.description: Phillips sends a last call without reply as the power fails, and the operators leave the cabin.
events.note: Bride (Q16566–16580) read directly: the power was failing and he did not think they were getting a spark. Bride put it about ten minutes before the end; Halpern gives 2:07 to 2:10.

events.title: The bow plunges; the bridge goes under
events.description: The bow takes a sudden plunge and the sea sweeps over the bridge and the forward Boat deck. The crow's nest is about level with the water. The lights are still burning.
events.note: Lightoller (US Inquiry p. 90–91; Q14052) and Chief Baker Joughin, who read a quarter past two on his watch with the lights on (Q6040–6049), as cited by Halpern, who derives a trim of 10°. Fitch, Layton and Wormstedt give 2:15; Halpern's table 2:17.

events.title: The forward funnel falls
events.description: The forward funnel falls, close to the overturned collapsible B.
events.note: The event is established; no source gives its minute. It followed the floating off of collapsible B at about 2:15. Mengot and Woytowich attribute it to the stays parting as the forward expansion joint opened. The time shown is the project's placement within that interval.

events.title: The lights go out
events.description: All the ship's lights go out, two to three minutes before the stern disappears. From the Californian the steamer's lights are seen to disappear at the same moment.
events.note: Symons (Q11510–11525) as cited by Halpern; Gibson on the Californian (Q7565: five past two by her wheelhouse clock) read directly. The report says the lights "kept alight practically until the last".

events.title: The hull breaks apart
events.description: The hull fails abaft amidships. The stern settles back toward the water, then tips up again as the flooding bow drags its forward end down.
events.location: Between the third funnel and the reciprocating engine room
events.note: Timing derived from the lights going out. The break is confirmed by the wreck; its mechanics follow the Marine Forensics Panel reconstruction (failure starting in the bottom structure at about 15 to 17° of trim).

alternatives.position: The ship sank intact: "The ship did not break in two".

events.title: The stern rises
events.description: The stern section rises to a steep angle and remains afloat for a few minutes at most.
events.note: Symons and Dillon as cited by Halpern. The angle reached is not known: the Marine Forensics Panel states that it cannot be determined; published figures range from about 30° to perpendicular.

events.title: The ship founders
events.description: The stern disappears below the surface, two hours and forty minutes after the collision.
events.note: "Disappeared at 2.20 a.m." (British report); independent watch readings.

events.title: The bow section reaches the seabed
events.description: The bow section strikes the bottom about 3,800 metres down, burying its stem in the sediment.
events.location: Seabed, about 600 m from the stern section
events.note: Mengot describes a descent of about five minutes; published estimates give five to six minutes for a fall of about 3,800 m. The clock time is the project's computation from those durations.

events.title: The stern section reaches the seabed
events.description: The stern section, falling almost vertically and probably rotating, strikes the bottom near the boilers that fell from the break.
events.note: No source gives a duration specific to the stern; the same five to six minutes is assumed by the project.
